'''''Rhamnus crocea''''', the '''spiny redberry''', is a species of plant in the family [[Rhamnaceae]]. It is native from [[California]] to northern [[Mexico]]. {{As of|2024|March}}, five subspecies are recognized.<ref name=POWO_718294-1/>

==Description==
This [[evergreen]] shrub is typically {{Convert|1-2|m|ft|frac=2}} in height.<ref>{{cite book|first=LeRoy|last=Abrams|year=1951|title=Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States|publisher=Stanford University Press|volume=3|isbn=0-8047-0005-2|page=63|url=https://archive.org/details/illustratedflora03abra/page/62/mode/2up}}</ref> The leaves are {{Convert|1.4|cm|frac=8}} long. The flowers have four yellow-green [[sepals]] and no petals. The fruit is a red berry containing two nutlets.<ref name="tktimb">{{Cite book |last1=Turner |first1=Mark |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VLbAAwAAQBAJ |title=Trees & Shrubs of the Pacific Northwest |last2=Kuhlmann |first2=Ellen |date=2014 |publisher=[[Timber Press]] |isbn=978-1-60469-263-1 |edition=1st |location=Portland, OR |pages=234}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Rhamnus crocea'' is [[Native species|native]] to [[Arizona]], [[California]], [[Nevada]], and [[Oregon]] in the United States and to [[:Category:Flora of Northeastern Mexico|Northeastern]] and [[:Category:Flora of Northwestern Mexico|Northwestern Mexico]] and the [[:Category:Flora of Mexican Pacific Islands|Mexican Pacific Islands]].<ref name=POWO_718294-1/> It covers two major mountain foothills. In California, it surrounds the entire [[San Joaquin Valley]], the pacific coast ranges and the western foothills of the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra Nevada]]s. In Arizona, it is found in the entire length of the [[Mogollon Rim]] to the western region of the [[White Mountains (Arizona)|White Mountains]].<ref name="Little">{{cite book|first=Elbert L.|last=Little Jr.|title=Atlas of United States Trees|volume=3 (Minor Western Hardwoods)|year=1976|publisher=US Government Printing Office|lccn=79-653298|oclc=4053799|entry-url=https://archive.org/details/atlasofunitedsta1314litt/page/n231/mode/2up|entry=Map 150, ''R. crocea''}}</ref>

''R. crocea'' typically occurs in [[chaparral]], with common flora associates being [[toyon]] and [[hollyleaf cherry]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Hogan |first=C. Michael |year=2008 |editor-last=Stromberg |editor-first=N. |title=Toyon (Heteromeles arbutifolia) |url=http://globaltwitcher.auderis.se/artspec_information.asp?thingid=84109&lang=us |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090719220426/http://globaltwitcher.auderis.se/artspec_information.asp?thingid=84109&lang=us |archive-date=July 19, 2009 |website=GlobalTwitcher}}</ref>

==Uses==
The edible fruit<ref name="tktimb" /> was consumed by Native Americans in the Western United States.<ref name="Saunders">{{cite book|first=Charles Francis|last=Saunders|year=1934|title=Edible and Useful Wild Plants|publisher=Dover|lccn=75-46193|isbn=978-0-486-23310-9|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yMw9DwAAQBAJ&q=Rhamnus%20crocea&pg=PA91|page=91}}</ref> When eaten in large quantities, it reportedly imparts a red tint to the consumer's entire body.<ref name="Saunders" />
